title: Introduction to hvtiRpropensity
text: practice propensity score estimated covariates matching weighting. ps_logistic() fits stats::glm(..., family = binomial()) appends several columns mirror original SAS template output: scored dataset can passed directly ps_match() ps_weight(). SAS template fits model separately imputed dataset (PROC LOGISTIC ... _IMPUTATION_) averages predicted probabilities PROC SUMMARY mean=. Pass stacked long-format MI data frame set imputation_col replicate . ordered treatment variables (e.g. NYHA functional class / II / III–IV), ps_ordinal() fits proportional-odds cumulative logit model via MASS::polr(), equivalent default PROC LOGISTIC behaviour ordinal responses SAS. SAS template decomposes cumulative probabilities marginal probabilities: p1 = col1; p2 = col2 - col1; p3 = 1 - col2. ps_ordinal() performs decomposition internally, appending one prob_<level> column per level. unordered multi-level treatments (e.g. repair type: CE / COS / PER / DEV), ps_nominal() fits generalised logit model via nnet::multinom(), equivalent SAS PROC LOGISTIC ... / link=glogit. first factor level reference category (REF=first SAS); use ref_level override.

Extreme IPTW weights inflate variance can dominate estimates. sa_trim_sweep() sweeps range winsorisation thresholds reports ESS weight distribution change. what: hvtiRpropensity: Propensity Score Methods for Cardiac Surgery Studies — hvtiRpropensity-package
title: hvtiRpropensity: Propensity Score Methods for Cardiac Surgery Studies — hvtiRpropensity-package
text: Provides functions propensity score balancing score analysis used cardiac surgery comparative-effectiveness research.  Translates Cleveland Clinic HVTI SAS template library consistent R workflow. Step 1 — estimate scores (new version): ps_logistic() — binary treatment propensity score (logistic regression; supports multiply-imputed data via stacked data frame). ps_ordinal() — ordered treatment propensity score (proportional-odds model via MASS::polr; equivalent SAS PROC LOGISTIC default ordinal responses). ps_nominal() — nominal treatment propensity score (multinomial logistic via nnet::multinom; equivalent SAS PROC LOGISTIC link=glogit). bs_continuous() — balancing score continuous exposure (linear regression; equivalent SAS PROC REG + %grp macro). bs_count() — balancing score count exposure (negative-binomial Poisson regression; equivalent SAS PROC GENMOD dist=nb). Step 2 — balance use scores: ps_match() — 1:1 nearest-neighbour matching pre-computed score. Returns pair_id column $data use sa_rosenbaum(). ps_weight() — IPTW weights (ATE / ATT / ATC) pre-computed score.
